notes.title: Ryder has launched!
notes.notes:
[p]It’s finally here! After three years of building, designing, and dreaming, Ryder is out in the world.[/p][p]This is a peaceful, creature-filled adventure where you’ll:[/p][list][*][p]Solve nearly 100 unique puzzles[/p][/*][*][p]Explore 4 colorful regions, from autumn forests to frozen peaks[/p][/*][*][p]Bond with over 60 creatures and become them[/p][/*][*][p]Unlock unique abilities like wind jumping, ice bridges, and more[/p][/*][*][p]Watch the world fill with sound and life as you restore it[/p][/*][/list][p]Whether you’re here for the cozy vibes, the curious creatures, or just something a little different, we hope Ryder gives you a quiet place to explore and reflect.[/p][p]We’re a team of two, and Ryder has been our dream for a long time. If you decide to take this journey, we hope it feels special to you as well.[/p][p]Thank you for playing.
Elle & Arlin[/p][p][/p][p]Please note: Ryder is fully functional on the Steamdeck but it needs to be launched with DirectX 11. This may be helpful if you are on a lower-spec configuration as well.
Here's how to do that:

1) Click the gear icon from Ryder's library page[/p][p]2) Click to "Properties"
3) Add -dx11 to the launch options field[/p][p]4) It should now launch no problem :)[/p]

notes.title: Glow Up - The Thundershroom Variant
notes.notes:
Deep within Sapphire Grove, something beautiful is taking root.

The forest’s glowing mushrooms have started leaving their mark — not just on the trees and stones, but on the creatures themselves. These are the Thundershroom variants: visually distinct forms that shimmer with white and gold energy, as if they've been shaped by the same mysterious glow that lights up the grove at night.

They shimmer like the caps of the grove’s bioluminescent fungi. They’re rare, but not out of reach — and discovering them adds a little magic to your time in the grove.

Every creature in Sapphire Grove has a Thundershroom form to find.

notes.title: Solving Puzzles in Ryder: How Do Pressure Plates Work?
notes.notes:
Happy March, everyone! 🌿 As we continue developing Ryder, we want to dive deeper into the puzzle mechanics that shape your journey. This month, we're breaking down Pressure Plates—one of the core mechanics you'll encounter while solving environmental puzzles.

[b]What Are Pressure Plates?[/b]
Pressure Plates are interactive switches that activate when a certain amount of weight is applied. They can open gates, move platforms, or activate other mechanics, but not every plate is the same! Some require only lightweight creatures, while others demand something much heavier to press them down fully.

Since Ryder lets you become different creatures, your choice of form directly impacts how you interact with pressure plates. Here’s how:

[b]Light Creatures [/b] – Can press smaller plates, but is not heavy enough for larger ones.
[b]Medium Creatures[/b] – Balance between agility and weight, useful for stepping on medium pressure plates [b]or light pressure plates.
Heavy Creatures[/b] – Can activate large pressure plates that smaller creatures can’t.
[b]Extra Heavy Creatures [/b]– Slow and steady but can activate the largest pressure plates and all other sized pressure plates.

Some puzzles will require multiple creatures working together, meaning you’ll need to swap between forms strategically to keep a plate activated while moving forward!

notes.title: Masters of the Chill
notes.notes:
[b]Happy New Year, All! [/b]

As we kickoff 2025 and the snow starts to fall outside, we thought it would be a great time to highlight the creature abilities in Ryder’s snowy region, the Silver Pines. 

The Silver Pines is a region covered by ever present frost and snow. Here, you will unlock creatures that harness the power of the cold, the Freeze and Ice Bridge abilities.

[b]The Freeze Ability[/b]

When using a creature with the Freeze ability, you can temporarily encase objects in ice, halting its position. This can come in handy when you need to be able to use the orb power in two places at once. For example, keeping the gate open so you may pass through without powering it with an orb.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45278192/d865f17d5aaf2e0a763aff0308238a110d706ee8.gif[/img]

[b]The Ice Bridge Ability[/b]

The Ice Bridge ability creates a temporary pathway across gaps, allowing fellow creatures to cross. The catch? The creator of the bridge must remain in place to hold it, adding a layer of teamwork and planning to every use as you navigate through the puzzle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45278192/f08a35c71d4c53f655f56f1b1b7a7218c034167d.gif[/img]

The Silver Pines is more than a wintry landscape—it’s a realm of challenges that demand creativity and patience. With the Freeze and Ice Bridge abilities, you’ll transform obstacles into opportunities, forging your path through this frigid wonderland and bringing back to life its creatures within.

Be sure to wishlist Ryder on Steam and follow us on our social channels for more Ryder news and to hear about when the demo is live!

notes.title: Meet the husband and wife duo behind Ryder
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! We’re Arlin and Elle at Yellow Tree Games. We're a husband-and-wife team united by our shared love for art, programming, and video games. Through this passion, we created Ryder, a creature-collecting puzzle adventure with a world brimming with unique, fantastical creatures.

[h1][b]Crafting a Vision for Ryder[/b][/h1]
The idea for Ryder began with a simple goal: a low-poly creature-collecting game that felt as distinct as it was immersive. Elle’s love for drawing animals and our mutual appreciation for classic creature-collecting games steered us in this direction from the start. Our goal was to create a nostalgic visual experience with a high level of detail, striking a balance between retro charm and modern design. We chose a low-poly art style rendered through Unreal Engine’s Lumen system, achieving both technical and artistic goals. Being a small team, we needed designs that were detailed enough to feel unique yet manageable enough to develop within a realistic timeframe. By focusing on each creature’s essentials, we can build a diverse and vibrant world without overstretching.

[h1][b]Shaping Ryder’s Core Gameplay[/b][/h1]
At the heart of Ryder are two core principles: each creature should add something new and distinct to gameplay, and collecting creatures should involve not just collecting, but understanding their utility. We experimented with different gameplay loops—survival, mini-games, racing, resource gathering, and even creature farming—before realizing that creature-driven puzzles best reflected our vision. Puzzles became the perfect way to spotlight each creature’s unique traits and give players meaningful interactions.
We also made a deliberate design choice to allow players to become the creatures themselves rather than just ride or mount them. This unique perspective lets players experience the world through each creature's eyes, with puzzles tailored to the physicality and abilities of every creature. This decision added depth to gameplay, letting players explore the world from different perspectives and engage with puzzles in a way that feels natural and satisfying.


[h1][b]Building a Creature-Rich Puzzle World[/b][/h1]
In Ryder, “distinct addition” means each creature offers unique trade-offs that shape the puzzle experience. For example, two creatures might share the same ability, but one might be as large as an elephant while the other is a small mouse. The elephant-sized creature can trigger weight-sensitive mechanisms, while the mouse can fit into narrow spaces. Ryder’s puzzles often require balancing these abilities, such as using a heavier creature to open a path and then switching to a smaller one to progress through tighter areas.
While puzzles are central to Ryder, we wanted the game to feel like an open, exploratory world rather than a series of back-to-back challenges. Players are encouraged to venture off the main path, uncover new creatures, and experience the freedom of roaming in the woods with their favorites. Our bestiary system allows hardcore collectors to hunt down every puzzle and creature, while casual players can advance through organic exploration at their own pace.


[h1][b]The Road to Release[/b][/h1]
We’re thrilled to be working toward a 2025 release, with plans to include over 60 creatures and more than 100 puzzles. Designing puzzles that work seamlessly with each creature’s traits has been a fun challenge, and we can’t wait to share more details on how these mechanics will unfold.
Thank you for following our journey with Ryder! We’ll dive deeper into the puzzle mechanics and other aspects of the game in upcoming dev logs. In the meantime, you can follow us on our social channels for sneak peeks and updates as we bring Ryder to life.

notes.title: Announcing Ryder!
notes.notes:
Hi everyone,

We're Arlin and Elle from Yellow Tree Games, and we're thrilled to finally share what we've been passionately working on for the past few years—[b][i]Ryder[/i][/b]!

[i][b]Ryder [/b][/i]is a creature-collecting puzzle adventure set in a stylized low-poly world. You play as a Ryder—an ethereal being with the ability to inhabit living creatures through a process known as [b]bonding[/b]. Your journey takes you to the summit of the Sanguine Mountain, but between you and your destiny lie three distinct regions filled with intricate puzzles.

At the outset, you'll find the world empty of life. By solving [b]Sacred Site[/b] puzzles, you'll restore the souls of creatures hidden away long ago. Each puzzle involves moving orbs blocked by environmental mechanics like gates, weighted pressure plates, and moving platforms. Strategically switch between your party of creatures to get the orbs to their destinations and bring life back to the world.

[b]Check out our reveal trailer here:[/b]
[previewyoutube=pv5teT2ifxA;full][/previewyoutube]

Explore open levels, discover special collectibles, rare creature variants, and other secrets as you complete your bestiary and learn more about the world of Ryder. Each region concludes with the release of a Divine Creature, unlocked by solving larger, more complex puzzles that incorporate everything you've learned.

After freeing all three Divine Creatures, the temple at the peak of the Sanguine Mountain will be unlocked, and your final ascent awaits where your destiny lies. In the end, you'll have solved over [b]100 puzzles[/b], played as more than [b]60 creatures[/b], and restored life to the regions once again, fulfilling your destiny as a Ryder.

We're aiming to launch Ryder in [b]2025[/b]. Until then, we'll be sharing updates and behind-the-scenes content regularly.

If you haven't already, please add Ryder to your Steam Wishlist!

Thank you for joining us on this journey. We can't wait for you to experience Ryder!

Warm Regards,
Arlin and Elle
